A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PaM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR, speaker-number verification, and audio-captioning experiments, including baseline comparisons and encoder-combination analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds captioning metrics, routing ablations, encoder and backbone comparisons, feature-similarity measurements, and prompt-generalization results.

M1.justification: The adopted PaM procedure retains multi-layer feature fusion, a shared expert plus one prompt-selected expert, and the same training losses. BEATs and alternative routing configurations are additional experiments within this framework. Revised indexing does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: The audio datasets and ASR, SNV, and captioning tasks remain unchanged. Appendix A.11 adds evaluation of previously unseen ASR prompt wording, extending coverage to a distinct instruction-input condition.

E2.justification: Table 11 introduces an evaluated audio-based MoE routing comparator, directly testing the central prompt-routing choice. Table 10 also adds WavLLM comparisons within the previously reported Qwen2.5-7B and LLaMA3.1-8B settings. The original main-table comparator set remains intact.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include FENSE, Sentence-BERT, CIDEr, and SPICE for captioning; a four-encoder BEATs configuration; controlled routing variants; and router evaluation on 200 ASR prompts, including 150 unseen prompts. The original training schedule, LoRA settings, and decoding procedure are retained in Appendix A.6.

E4.justification: Table 11 adds audio-based routing, one-expert, no-shared-expert, and no-task-label comparisons. Appendix A.9 adds cross-encoder feature-similarity analysis, and A.11 tests unseen-prompt routing. BEATs and larger-LLM comparisons further extend the existing configuration analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. Average ranks and averages across encoder combinations do not constitute run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The retained result tables match numerically after renumbering and formatting changes. Substantial new results cover additional metrics, BEATs, larger-LLM baselines, routing ablations, and feature similarity. For example, Table 8 reports BEATs-variant SNV accuracy of 49.2% versus 42.8%, alongside worse AMI WER of 13.11 versus 12.79. These compare configurations, not improved reruns of the original model.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the formal layer-state definitions, summation bounds, and fusion-matrix dimensions in Equations 4–6, including changing the stated matrix shape from 3 × (L1 + L2 + L3) to K × sum(Li − 1). No theorem or proof is added; inconsistencies between the prose and summation indices remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central prompt-aware fusion and multitask-performance claims. The introduction newly makes an explicit performance claim that audio-only routing produces suboptimal results, referencing Table 11, whereas v1 only identifies its lack of prompt conditioning.

C2.justification: Appendices A.7–A.9 add substantive interpretations of backbone-dependent concatenation failures, task-specific shared-expert tradeoffs, and feature mismatch when initializing from multimodal LLMs. Section 5 also replaces v1's asserted applicability to unseen tasks with a proposal requiring future validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a planned code-repository address, caption-evaluation tool and model details, and an explicit model-loading workaround in A.4. Section 4.5 newly specifies activated and per-expert parameter counts, and A.11 supplies more prompt examples. Existing training hyperparameters are relocated without substantive changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Soundwave and references concerning multimodal models, task-level routing, initialization, and decoding efficiency. It removes some general scaling background citations. These extend the context while retaining the core positioning around task-specific multi-encoder fusion.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. v2 edits terminology and fusion explanations, rewrites the discussion, condenses related work, and moves prompt examples, dataset details, and training settings into reorganized appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial experimental displays in Tables 7–12 and prompt tables 14–16. Figure 2 gains explicit feature, routing, and FFN labels; Figure 1's caption and Figure 4's direction labels are revised. Existing tables and Figure 3 are also relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important evidential gap: Table 11 directly tests prompt routing, task supervision, and shared experts, whose contributions v1 did not isolate. Additional metrics and backbone comparisons strengthen evaluation and expose meaningful limitations. These gains substantially improve the empirical justification despite remaining equation/editorial inconsistencies and the continued absence of run-to-run uncertainty.
